static.title: Squeezing the Sun
static.note: The Sun keeps all of its mass. Only its size changes. The gauge is the ordinary escape speed from the surface, worked out the way you would for a planet.

presets.label: The Sun today
presets.note: 696,000 km across the radius. Escape speed 618 km/s, which is about two ten-thousandths of the speed of light.

presets.label: Earth-sized
presets.note: A whole solar mass packed into a ball the size of the Earth. This is roughly what a white dwarf is.

presets.label: 30 km
presets.note: A solar mass in a ball the size of a city. This is roughly a neutron star, and light now needs about a third of its speed to get away.

presets.label: 6 km
presets.note: Twice the Schwarzschild radius. The escape speed is already seven tenths of the speed of light.

presets.label: 3 km
presets.note: The Schwarzschild radius of one solar mass, 2.95 km. The Newtonian escape speed here comes out at exactly the speed of light.

static.title: Average density, on a ladder
static.note: This is the black hole’s mass divided by the volume of a sphere the size of its event horizon. It is a comparison number, not a claim about what the inside is made of. Every small tick on the ladder is ten times denser than the one below it.

static.title: Densidad media, en una escalera
static.note: This is the black hole’s mass divided by the volume of a sphere the size of its event horizon. It is a comparison number, not a claim about what the inside is made of. Every small tick on the ladder is ten times denser than the one below it.

static.title: Counting the zeros
static.note: Start from a 10 M☉ black hole and multiply its mass. Each bar shows how many zeros that quantity gained, or lost. Radius grows in step with mass, so volume grows three times as fast, and density has to fall.

static.title: Contando los ceros

static.title: How cold is it?
static.note: Quantum physics predicts that a black hole behaves as though it has a temperature. Every small tick on this thermometer is ten times hotter than the one below it, so a short drop on screen is an enormous drop in temperature.
